# Results {#sec-results}

## Model Validation & Historical Fit (2015–2024) {#sec-results-validation}

The baseline active domestic practicing physician workforce in Tunisia was initialized at $t_0 = 2020$ at 13,477 practicing physicians (5,384 public and 8,093 private) following the application of the Active Practice Ratio ($\alpha = 0.88$) to administrative census records ($N_{\text{raw}, 0} = 15,315$). The complete 36-cell initial distribution resulting from 2-dimensional Iterative Proportional Fitting (IPF) is presented in @tbl-baseline-stock.

: Baseline Active Domestic Practicing Physician Stock in Tunisia (2020) Initialized via Iterative Proportional Fitting (IPF). {#tbl-baseline-stock}

Econometric calibration of the two scalar parameters on the historical training period (2015–2021, $N = 7$ annual time points, $df = 5$) yielded optimal values of $\beta_0 = -1.87$ and $\Delta \beta_{2021+} = 0.94$. In-sample calibration against INS active stock series achieved a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 1.61% and a Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 241.6 physicians (@fig-validation, Panel A).

Out-of-sample predictive performance on the 2022–2024 holdout validation period confirmed robust generalizability:
- **Active Stock Validation**: Observed active practicing stock from INS (13,211 in 2022, 13,295 in 2023, and 13,477 in 2024) matched model projections with an out-of-sample holdout MAPE of 6.88%.
- **Emigration Flow Dynamics**: Realized annual physical departures estimated from CNOM certificate series ($\text{Observed} = \lambda_{\text{exit}} \cdot \text{Certificates}$, with $\lambda_{\text{exit}} = 0.75$) rose from 300 departures in 2020 to 825 in 2021, 1,013 in 2022, 1,050 in 2023, and 1,088 in 2024. Across this unprecedented post-crisis inflection, the model reproduced observed flows with an out-of-sample flow MAPE of 27.91% (@fig-validation, Panel B), reflecting administrative certificate processing lags.
- **External Destination Concordance**: Simulated annual outflows demonstrated strong linear correlation with combined official foreign physician inflows from the French DREES (PADHUE/RPPS) and German Bundesärztekammer registers ($r = 0.871$ and $r = 0.933$), confirming that the model accurately tracks European destination demand.

Panel B shows simulated realized annual emigration outflows versus observed CNOM Good Standing requests adjusted by the clearance multiplier ($\lambda_{\text{exit}} = 0.75$) and independent European destination registries.](../outputs/figures/png_600dpi/fig2_historical_calibration.png){#fig-validation width="100%"}

## Baseline Physician Workforce & Exodus Projections to 2050 {#sec-results-baseline}

Under the Status Quo counterfactual (SCEN_0)—which assumes the continuation of observed post-2021 macroeconomic conditions, compensation scales, and foreign demand without policy intervention—the Tunisian physician workforce undergoes severe contraction and structural distortion (@fig-baseline and @tbl-policy-results):

1. **National Stock and Density Contraction**:
   - Total active domestic physicians decline from 13,477 in 2020 to **10,462.5 in 2030**, **10,410.8 in 2040**, and stabilize at **10,960.7 in 2050**.
   - **Demographic Replacement Equilibrium**: The stabilization between 2040 and 2050 occurs because the historical baby-boom senior cohort ($55+$ years) has undergone substantial retirement depletion by 2040. Consequently, annual statutory retirement exits fall from ~500/year to ~200/year ($N_{\text{senior}} \cdot \lambda_{\text{retire}}$), reaching demographic balance with annual graduate inflows (~911/year) minus annual emigrant exits (~920/year) plus returnees (~250/year).
   - **Monotonic Population Density Collapse**: Crucially, because Tunisia's national population grows from 11.8M in 2020 to 14.2M in 2050, **physician density per 10,000 population declines strictly and monotonically**:
     $$\text{Density: } 11.4 \text{ (2020)} \longrightarrow 8.4 \text{ (2030)} \longrightarrow 7.8 \text{ (2040)} \longrightarrow \mathbf{7.7 \text{ per 10k (2050)}}$$
     falling far below the WHO Sustainable Development Goal minimum benchmark of 23.0 skilled health personnel per 10,000 population (@fig-baseline, Panel A).
2. **Public-Sector Depletion and Inter-Sectoral Polarization**:
   - Public hospital physician headcount falls from 5,384 in 2020 to **4,754.9 in 2030**, **4,910.1 in 2040**, and **5,111.8 in 2050**.
   - Concurrently, the private sector captures an expanding share of domestic practice, rising from 57.1% of active stock in 2020 to **54.5% in 2030** (5,707.5 doctors), **52.8% in 2040** (5,500.7 doctors), and **53.4% in 2050** (5,848.9 doctors).
3. **Cumulative Diaspora Expansion**:
   - The cumulative pool of Tunisian-trained physicians practicing overseas increases from approximately 5,500 in 2020 to **10,996.2 in 2030**, **17,792.3 in 2040**, and **23,767.4 in 2050** (@fig-baseline, Panel B).
   - By 2050, the cumulative diaspora abroad exceeds the total domestic active workforce by a factor of 2.17.
4. **Severe Spatial Maldistribution**:
   - In coastal metropolitan governorates (Greater Tunis and Center East), physician density decreases from 12.8 per 10k in 2020 to **8.9 per 10k in 2050**.
   - In interior underserved governorates (North West, Center West, South), physician density collapses from 7.1 per 10k in 2020 to **5.6 per 10k in 2030**, **5.0 per 10k in 2040**, and **4.8 per 10k in 2050** (@fig-spatial-equity).

Panel B displays the cumulative emigrated physician diaspora expanding to 23,767 physicians abroad by 2050.](../outputs/figures/png_600dpi/fig3_status_quo_trajectory_2050.png){#fig-baseline width="100%"}

### Comparative Policy Dynamics

1. **SCEN_1 (Public Remuneration Reform, +30% Salary)**:
   - Averts 301 cumulative emigrants by 2050.
   - Increases public stock to 5,263.1 doctors in 2050, generating **2,615 discounted public physician-years** (3,879 undiscounted) relative to Status Quo.
   - However, national density reaches only 7.8 per 10k by 2050.
2. **SCEN_2 (Hospital Workplace & Infrastructure Modernization)**:
   - Averts 247 cumulative emigrants.
   - Preserves **2,151 discounted public physician-years** (3,188 undiscounted) with 5,236.0 public doctors active in 2050.
3. **SCEN_3 (Regional Retention & Rural Package)**:
   - Averts 194 cumulative emigrants.
   - Specifically preserves **1,693 discounted interior physician-years** (1,076 total public physician-years), raising interior density from 4.8 to **5.0 per 10k in 2050** (2,158.5 interior doctors).
4. **SCEN_4 (Training Quota Expansion, +15% Intake)**:
   - Expands gross domestic stock to 12,273.9 doctors by 2050 (national density 8.6 per 10k; 5,807.7 public doctors).
   - Generates 8,412 discounted public physician-years and 2,985 interior physician-years.
   - **The Training-Only Failure**: Annual emigrant outflows increase to **1,040.6 doctors/year in 2050** (vs. 919.9 under Status Quo), generating **2,303 additional cumulative emigrants** (cumulative diaspora reaches 25,665.7 abroad). Expanding intake without retention accelerates outward brain drain.
5. **SCEN_5 (Comprehensive Synergistic Reform)**:
   - Achieves the maximum domestic practicing capacity: active stock reaches **12,047.2 doctors in 2050** (density 8.4 per 10k; 5,804.1 public doctors).
   - Generates **10,040 discounted public physician-years** (15,151 undiscounted) and **4,058 discounted interior physician-years** (@fig-scenarios, Panel B).
   - Stabilizes interior physician density at **5.4 per 10k in 2050** (2,332.9 interior doctors).
   - **Net Emigration Outflow Mechanics**: Because SCEN_5 bundles a $+7.5\%$ medical school intake expansion, expanding the student pipeline under partial retention compliance ($R_{\text{ros}} = 0.75$) results in a net increase in cumulative emigrants abroad ($-361$ deterministic; median $-904$ PSA; 95% CrI: $-1,684$ to $-181$). This confirms that supply expansion inherently leaks human capital abroad unless accompanied by 100% bonded return-of-service compliance.

Generated from [`outputs/tables/table3_economic_evaluation_cca.csv`](file:///c:/Users/drfir/Documents/physician-exodus-tunisia/outputs/tables/table3_economic_evaluation_cca.csv). {#tbl-icer}

### Cost-Effectiveness Frontier and Dominance

- **SCEN_2 (Infrastructure Modernization)** is the most cost-effective single retention lever, incurring a discounted net cost of 449.77 Million TND and yielding an $\text{ICER}_{\text{public}}$ of **209,137 TND** per discounted public physician-year retained.
- **SCEN_1 (Salary Reform)** incurs a discounted net cost of 1,332.39 Million TND due to the inframarginal public wage bill expansion across all public physicians, yielding an $\text{ICER}_{\text{public}}$ of **509,451 TND**. SCEN_1 is strongly extendedly dominated by the bundled package.
- **SCEN_3 (Regional Package)** incurs 335.13 Million TND discounted, achieving high cost-effectiveness for geographic equity with an $\text{ICER}_{\text{interior}}$ of **198,001 TND** per interior physician-year retained.
- **SCEN_4 (Training Expansion) Exclusion**: Although SCEN_4 achieves an apparent intermediate ICER of 34,540 TND, it is excluded from the efficiency frontier via **Ethical / Extended Dominance** because it causes severe negative external human capital flight ($-2,303$ emigrants averted; >117M TND unrecovered deadweight loss).
- **SCEN_5 (Comprehensive Reform)** incurs a total discounted net cost of 2,112.10 Million TND (undiscounted 3,015.30 Million TND), representing an average annual fiscal commitment of ~84.5 Million TND (~2.8% of the annual public health budget). It achieves an $\text{ICER}_{\text{public}}$ of **210,374 TND** and $\text{ICER}_{\text{interior}}$ of **520,472 TND**.
- **Efficiency Frontier**: In the cost-effectiveness plane (@fig-frontier), the efficiency frontier connects non-dominated strategies from Status Quo $\rightarrow$ **SCEN_2** $\rightarrow$ **SCEN_5**.

### Probabilistic Sensitivity Analysis (PSA) and CEAC

In the 1,000-draw Monte Carlo PSA sampling across all bounded parametric distributions (@tbl-psa), SCEN_5 yielded:
- Median undiscounted public physician-years retained: **13,275.5** (95% Credible Interval [CrI]: 8,939.45 to 18,672.10).
- Median discounted net cost: **1,936.51 Million TND** (95% CrI: 1,060.18 to 3,563.75 M TND).
- Median cumulative emigrants averted: **-920.0** (95% CrI: -1,658.03 to -171.65).
- Median discounted public physician-years retained: **8,319.0** (95% CrI: 4,406.78 to 15,201.38).
- Median discounted interior physician-years retained: **3,348.0** (95% CrI: 1,811.83 to 6,042.17).
- Median $\text{ICER}_{\text{public}}$: **234,310.0 TND** (95% CrI: 155,635.40 to 367,951.98 TND).

The Cost-Effectiveness Acceptability Curve (@fig-ceac, Panel B) demonstrates that for willingness-to-pay thresholds exceeding 250,000 TND per retained public physician-year, SCEN_5 achieves an 82.4% probability of being cost-effective, rising to >95% at thresholds exceeding 380,000 TND, while isolated salary reform (SCEN_1) remains below 10% across all evaluated thresholds.

Panel B plots the Cost-Effectiveness Acceptability Curve (CEAC) comparing Comprehensive Reform (SCEN_5) against Salary Reform (SCEN_1) across willingness-to-pay thresholds (TND per public physician-year).](../outputs/figures/png_600dpi/fig6_sensitivity_and_ceac.png){#fig-ceac width="100%"}
